Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the thoughtful conversation earlier today. Per our call, attached is a revised renewal proposal with three structure options so your procurement and finance teams can evaluate trade-offs quickly:

- Option A: 1-year renewal, standard annual pricing, no ramp commitments.
- Option B: 2-year agreement with a staged ramp (Q1 +25% capacity, Q2 +50%, Q4 full run-rate) and a 12% multi-year discount.
- Option C: 3-year co-term with your existing vendor agreement, built-in cost smoothing and 18% multiyear discount.

Key asks we heard from you: remove the automatic renewal clause, align co-terming to your fiscal calendar (co-terming window: Oct 1), and provide clear breakpoints where capacity increases trigger pricing caps. The attached SOW_ramp_schedule.xlsx shows the ramp milestones and billing treatment.

Karthik —

Thanks for the fast follow-up and the clear options. A few clarifications from Procurement before we engage legal: 

- Auto-renew: we will not accept an auto-renew that automatically charges the next term without a formal renewal confirmation. We need an explicit renewal/opt-in or a manual renewal window.
- Co-terming: we prefer co-terming if it keeps billing on the same Oct 1 cycle; however we need to see the math on how you allocate credit for the portion of the current year.
- Ramp schedule: we like staged ramping but need firm breakpoints and a cap on price increases if we exceed committed capacity.

Can you confirm whether Option B can be modified to remove auto-renew and include a break clause at 18 months? Also please provide a version with explicit per-unit pricing at each ramp milestone (so our FP&A can model).

If possible, include a suggested DocuSign flow for a co-term arrangement that preserves our audit trail.

Laura Jenkins
